newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 - PORLA reported CPO production in August rose 12.2 percent or 88,200 tonnes to 810,550 tonnes. This is slightly higher than our estimate of 801,000 tonnes. The better production performance reflected mainly the vigorous recovery in output in East Malaysia which saw a phenomenal increase of 34.7 percent or 44,300 tonnes to 172,200 tonnes. This represents half of the increase for the country. On an annual basis, production in August posted a growth rate of 15.4 percent. For the first eight months this year, production expanded 7.4 percent or 361,000 tonnes to 5.231 million tonnes.

Peninsular Malaysia alone accounted for 74 percent of the increase when its output grew seven percent to 4.08 million tonnes. Latest partial data for first-half-September indicated a slowdown in the seasonal production in both the Peninsular and in East Malaysia. The performance of several major producers in Peninsular Malaysia ranged from down two percent to up five percent. For the whole country, our tentative estimate for September shows production rising moderately by some 50,000 tonnes or six percent to 860,000 tonnes.

With production exceeding offtake, end August stocks of palm oil posted an increase of 45,000 tonnes to 800,900 tonnes. This compared with our estimate of 775,000 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone rose 69,500 tonnes to 472,200 tonnes. East Malaysia accounted for 51 percent of the increase when its CPO stocks rose 35,500 tonnes to 112,500 tonnes. PORLA reported smaller than expected August palm oil exports of 638,600 tonnes. This is lower than the July exports of 662,000 tonnes which was revised upward by 16,000 tonnes.

We view the preliminary August exports figure as understated and would not be surprised to see an upward revision to 675,000 tonnes. Palm oil exports remain good this month and should be higher than PORLA's preliminary August figure. Indonesia took 20,000 tonnes RBD olein during September 1-20 against nothing in August. From a low of 1,024 ringgit on July 11 CPO futures advanced to 1,100 ringgit in August 9. Thereafter in KLCE, just over three weeks price surged to an intraday high of 1,268 ringgit before settling at 1,249 ringgit on September 2.

This represents a gain of 225 ringgit in about seven weeks. However over the last two weeks the market had surrendered 114 ringgit or half the gains accumulated in the period between July 11 and early September. Better than expected palm production coupled with perceptions of a slowdown in offtake had generated heavy long liquidation as well as short selling by commission houses on the KLCE. We still view the price retracement as healthy and timely as it would restore the competitiveness of palm oil in the export market, not only against other oils but also against Indonesian palm oil.
December CPO futures settled at 1,137 ringgit last Friday. November/December RBD olein was quoted at $527.50.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).
